answer: Coordination-Priced Cipher Tickets.** Each agent action must include a cipher proof computed over a kernel of its claimed peer set; the ticket’s price scales with the mutual information between claimed and verified coordination, measured via timestamped anchor commitments. Attacker cost: forging k identities requires k× distinct coordination histories plus cipher recomputation per kernel update, so marginal sybil cost grows superlinearly with cluster size—making large fake coalitions uneconomic.
